svg.aria-label: The four Diffie-Hellman combinations in the WireGuard handshake and what each proves
svg.text: Each side has two key pairs: a permanent one (its identity) and a temporary one (just for this handshake)
lets Bob seal his identity before hearing a word back
only Bob and the Pi, the real ones, can compute this
forward secrecy: gone for ever once the keys are deleted
even a thief with the Pi’s private key can’t pretend to be Bob

figure.figcaption: The four X25519 exchanges in WireGuard’s handshake, in the order they happen. Each result is mixed into the keys, so the keys are safe as long as any one of them is.
